extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: A comprehensive benchmark of 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines (Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering) across 30 subjects and 183 subfields, designed to evaluate expert-level multimodal understanding and reasoning capabilities.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.publisher: IN.AI Research, University of Waterloo, The Ohio State University, Carnegie Mellon University, University of Victoria, Princeton University
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was collected through a three-stage process: (1) selecting 30 college subjects from six disciplines based on whether multimodal questions are commonly used, (2) recruiting collectors to gather questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, and (3) collecting 11.5K meticulously curated multimodal questions spanning these subjects.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: College exams, quizzes, and textbooks from 30 subjects across six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions were manually collected by a team of 50 college students (including coauthors) from various disciplines and subjects, drawing from online sources, textbooks, and lecture materials. Annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution. They were advised to select questions without immediately available answers. The process involved three stages: (1) selecting 30 subjects from six disciplines based on whether visual inputs are commonly adopted, (2) recruiting university students specializing in these majors to collect multimodal questions from textbooks and online resources or create new questions based on their expertise, (3) quality control through lexical overlap and URL similarity checks for duplicates, format and typo checking by co-authors, and categorizing problems into four difficulty levels (very easy, easy, medium, hard), with very easy problems excluded.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Quality control was performed through duplicate detection using lexical overlap and source URL similarity, followed by manual review. Format and typo checking was conducted by co-authors. Problems were categorized into difficulty levels, with approximately 10% classified as very easy being excluded from the benchmark. Error analysis was conducted on 150 randomly sampled error instances from GPT-4V's predictions, analyzed by expert annotators who identified root causes based on their knowledge and golden explanations.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 college students (including coauthors) from various disciplines and subjects, specializing in the 30 majors covered by the benchmark. For human expert evaluation, 90 college senior students were selected to represent experts in the corresponding 30 subjects (3 student experts per subject).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: OCR by MMOCR and captioning by LLaVA-1.5 were used to provide recognized text information to text-only LLMs for evaluation purposes, not for creating the dataset annotations.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases in the dataset construction.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. The benchmark combines multiple-choice questions with concise open-ended questions to balance complexity and practicality, which may limit the scope of assessment.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for evaluating large multimodal models (LMMs) in the context of Expert AGI, assessing both basic perceptual skills and complex reasoning abilities across various professional domains at college-level subjects.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Subject selection based on visual input relevance, followed by recruitment of annotators for data collection across 30 subjects from six disciplines

However, we argue that strong performance on this benchmark should be a necessary criterion for an Expert AGI system... rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: Firstly, we go through the common university majors to decide what subjects should be included in our benchmark. The selection is based on the principle that visual inputs should be commonly adopted in the subjects to provide valuable information. Through this principle, we rule out a few subjects like law and linguistics because it is difficult to find enough relevant multimodal problems in these subjects.
